title: Installation of a Trim Air Zone Valve in the Ceiling Distribution Run
abstract: Installation of a trim air zone valve in the ceiling distribution run, including the duct clamp torque sequence, the electrical connection and the zone regulation operational test that releases the zone to service.

sections.purpose: This task installs one trim air zone valve in the ceiling distribution run on either the forward or the aft station, and does the operational test that releases the zone back to service.
sections.job_setup_note: The valve must be at the same standard as the aircraft, and the duct flange faces must be clean and undamaged before the valve is offered up. A distorted clamp band will not hold the joint at pressure and is replaced rather than re-used. Two persons are needed to lift the valve into the ceiling void.
sections.procedure: 1. Make sure that the packs are selected off and that the air conditioning system is depressurised. 2. Remove the blanking caps from the duct ends and clean the flange faces. 3. Do a detailed visual inspection of the duct clamps and replace any clamp with a distorted band. 4. Lift the valve into position with a second person and offer the outlet flange squarely to the duct. CAUTION: DO NOT FORCE THE VALVE INTO ALIGNMENT. IF THE FLANGE DOES NOT SIT FLAT, THE DUCT SUPPORT MUST BE ADJUSTED FIRST. 5. Fit the two duct clamps hand tight. 6. Torque the clamps in the sequence given on drawing D21601117401, in two stages. 7. Connect the electrical connector at the valve and remove the protective cap. WARNING: MAKE SURE THAT NO PERSON IS IN THE CEILING VOID WHEN THE SYSTEM IS PRESSURISED. 8. Install the closeout above the distribution run. 9. Pressurise the air conditioning system and do a leak check at the two clamped joints. 10. Do the trim air system operational test and install the ceiling panels in zone 254 and, for the aft station, in zone 291.
sections.close_out: Remove all tools and waste material from the ceiling void and confirm the count against the tool control record. Clear the technical log entry raised at removal. Record the valve serial number and the aircraft modification status on the component change record.

safety_precautions: Make sure that the packs are selected off.
Make sure that no person is in the ceiling void before pressurisation.
Do the tool count before the closeout is installed.

title: Installation of a Trim Air Zone Valve in the Ceiling Distribution Run

issue.reason: The job set-up now states that the clamp torque sequence is keyed to the sensor boss position and that the change request for the boss-less standard is registered and held.

abstract: Installation of a trim air zone valve in the ceiling distribution run, including the duct clamp torque sequence, the sensor harness connection where fitted and the zone regulation operational test.

sections.purpose: This task installs one trim air zone valve in the ceiling distribution run on either the forward or the aft station, and does the operational test that releases the zone back to service.
sections.job_setup_note: The valve must be at the same standard as the aircraft. A valve carrying a sensor boss must not be fitted to an aircraft whose duct has no boss aperture, and a valve without the boss must not be fitted to an aircraft that expects a duct-mounted sensor, because the zone would be left unsensed. Check the modification status on the aircraft record before you unpack the valve. The clamp torque sequence in step 6 is set against the boss position and is not a general sequence: it exists so that the flange is drawn down evenly on the side the boss weld sits. It is therefore re-issued whenever the boss standard changes. A publication change request covering the boss-less configuration is registered against this task and is deliberately held, so that the task is rewritten once when that standard is decided rather than twice.
sections.procedure: 1. Make sure that the packs are selected off and that the air conditioning system is depressurised. 2. Remove the blanking caps from the duct ends and clean the flange faces. 3. Do a detailed visual inspection of the duct clamps and replace any clamp with a distorted band. 4. Lift the valve into position with a second person and align the outlet flange with the boss aperture where one is fitted. CAUTION: DO NOT FORCE THE VALVE INTO ALIGNMENT. IF THE FLANGE DOES NOT SIT FLAT, THE DUCT SUPPORT MUST BE ADJUSTED FIRST. 5. Fit the two duct clamps hand tight. 6. Torque the clamps in the sequence given on drawing D21601117401, in two stages. 7. Connect the sensor harness at the boss where fitted and remove the identification tag. 8. Connect the electrical connector at the valve and remove the protective cap. WARNING: MAKE SURE THAT NO PERSON IS IN THE CEILING VOID WHEN THE SYSTEM IS PRESSURISED. 9. Install the closeout above the distribution run. 10. Pressurise the air conditioning system and do a leak check at the two clamped joints. 11. Do the trim air system operational test and record the zone response time. 12. Install the ceiling panels in zone 254 and, for the aft station, in zone 291.
sections.close_out: Remove all tools and waste material from the ceiling void and confirm the count against the tool control record. Clear the technical log entry raised at removal. Record the valve serial number and the aircraft modification status on the component change record.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Steps 4 and 7 apply to aircraft post MOD-153140 only. A held change request covers the boss-less configuration.

safety_precautions: Make sure that the packs are selected off.
Make sure that no person is in the ceiling void before pressurisation.
Do the tool count before the closeout is installed.
